name: NVIDIA
look: Single green accent on an otherwise monochrome page, two-mode surface rhythm, and hyper-angular 2px geometry throughout.

hero.title: The engine of modern AI
hero.sub: GPUs, interconnect and a software stack that has been maintained for two decades. The reason a model trains in days rather than months.

features.title: Silicon is the easy half
features.sub: The compilers, libraries and framework integrations are what turn a fast chip into a fast training run.

items.title: Tensor cores
items.body: Purpose-built matrix units, with mixed precision handled by the libraries rather than by you.

items.title: NVLink
items.body: Hundreds of gigabytes per second between GPUs, so a model larger than one card still trains.

items.title: Mature software
items.body: Two decades of compilers and libraries, still supporting hardware you bought years ago.

items.title: Containers
items.body: Pre-built images for every major framework, versioned against driver releases.

items.title: Reference designs
items.body: Validated rack-scale configurations, so procurement is a specification rather than a research project.

items.title: Developer tools
items.body: Profilers that show which kernel is slow and why, not just that something is.

showcases.title: The software is the moat
showcases.body: A fast chip with immature libraries is a slow system. Two decades of compiler and library work is why frameworks target this platform first and why hardware from several generations ago still receives updates.
points: Profilers that identify the slow kernel

showcases.title: Beyond training runs
showcases.body: The same acceleration underpins simulation, medical imaging, weather modelling and rendering. The training boom is the visible part of a much older workload set.

gallery.title: DEVELOPERS
gallery.sub: SDKs, containers, profilers and reference implementations.

testimonial.quote: We ran the same job on hardware two generations old and it still got driver updates. That longevity is worth more to our procurement team than peak numbers.
testimonial.name: Hiro Nakamura

pricing.title: PRICING
pricing.sub: Hardware through partners. Cloud instances by the hour.

tiers.name: Cloud
tiers.desc: Rent capacity when you need it.

items.q: Why does the software matter so much?
items.a: Because peak hardware numbers are only reachable through mature compilers and libraries. Frameworks target this platform first, which means fewer surprises in production.
Driver and library support spans multiple generations, so systems bought years ago continue to receive updates rather than being stranded.

items.q: Can I try before buying hardware?
items.a: Yes — hourly cloud instances on every major provider, running the same stack, so a benchmark on rented capacity predicts on-premise behaviour.

items.q: What is included in the enterprise branch?
items.a: A long-lived driver branch with backported fixes and no feature churn, which is what production clusters need rather than the latest release.

cta.title: Start on rented capacity
cta.sub: Benchmark on the same stack before committing to hardware.

notes: A single green accent carries every CTA, active state and decorative motif. Everything else is monochrome.
Two surface modes alternate in a predictable rhythm down the page: dark for hero and footer chapters, light for the body.
Geometry is hyper-angular — 2px on every interactive element. There are no pills, no rounded cards and no soft chrome.
One proprietary sans at two weights, scaled across a twelve-tier hierarchy from 10px utility text to 48px display.
Cards separate with hairline borders and soft-tinted backgrounds rather than shadows.
